newsitem.title: USA: U.S. industry output grew more slowly in September.
newsitem.headline: U.S. industry output grew more slowly in September.

text.p: Production by the nation's mines, factories and utilities grew more slowly in September, the Federal Reserve said on Thursday, partly because of a continued slowdown in the auto industry.

Total industrial output increased 0.2 percent last month after a revised 0.4 percent rise in August, as businesses eased back to 83.3 percent of their maximum operating capacity in September from 83.4 percent.
The report confirmed a deceleration in third-quarer economic activity, as the Fed said growth in industrial output slowed to 4.4 percent from the second quarter's 6.7 percent surge.

The Fed said that the rate of new-car assemblies fell for a second straight month during September, down to 6.5 million new cars a year from 6.7 million in August. Light-truck output also declined to 5.4 million a year from 5.6 million.
The auto industry is a major influence on total output. Excluding motor vehicles and parts, national industrial output was up 0.4 percent in September after a 0.5 percent August rise.
Among major categories of output, mining industries' production fell 0.2 percent last month after a sharp rise of 2.4 percent in August.
Output by utility companies was up 0.4 percent in September, much less than the 1.7 percent jump posted in August. Cooler weather reduced electricity demand for air conditioning.

Previously, the Fed said that August industrial output had risen more strongly, by 0.5 percent, but it revised that down. It also revised July output to show no gain from June after previously reporting a 0.1 percent rise.
Manufacturing industries raised production in September by 0.2 percent after a 0.1 percent August rise.

The Fed said that, among durable goods producers, there was a substantial decline in output of motor vehicles and parts. But that was more than offset by increased production of computers and office equipment, aerospace and transportation goods.
